_doc: ENDINGS BY BUILD (Steve 2026-10-14: "Each playstyle and godhood path, moral choice version should have its own ending."). paths.<tablePath>.<selector>.<moral> = { title?, lines: [closing lines said after the final's outcome], finals?: { <finalId>: [lines that REPLACE that final's outcome] } }. Lookup order for the locked ending key, most specific first: 'god:<godId>' > 'class:<path>/<subclass>' > 'class:<path>' > 'track:<track>' > the path's own light/dark finals (table-<path>.js, never in this file). A slot with nothing authored falls through to the next. Final ids per path: see table-<path>.js finals, plus 'hosts' (THE HOSTS, adds lines only) and 'poddemand' (adds lines only). Tokens: {name} {class} {god} {verb}. Morals: light, dark; grey for the relay only. Validate and list what's missing: node scripts/validate-table-endings.js --todo

light.title: THE SHOWRUNNER'S FINALE

audience: You hand the audience the microphone and walk off your own stage. It's the best cue you ever called. Trillions of viewers find out what it's like to be asked, and the show becomes the government without anyone quite deciding it should.
It works because you built it to work: every segment has an exit, every host has a replacement, and nobody holds the remote for long. The ratings dip. The constitution doesn't.
quiet: You spend the finale on people the show never booked. You give the unfilmed villages the good lighting. You give the dead the long shot. You give the quiet ones the last word, and you cut the music so it's the only sound.
The audience weeps in eleven dimensions. Nobody can find you in the footage. That was the point.

lines: Later, the galaxy will try to name the producer of the most-watched night in its history. The credits roll for an hour and list everyone in Haven, alphabetically. Your name is in there somewhere, between a beekeeper and a child.
{name} never takes a bow. At the fire that night, someone asks who ran the whole thing. Everyone looks at everyone else, and laughs, and that's the right answer.

dark.title: THE SHOWRUNNER'S CUT

audience: The audience speaks, and every word is one you wrote for it. You built the show so well that the galaxy can't tell the difference between being heard and being produced. Neither can you, most nights.
The government is a program now. You are its showrunner, uncredited and permanent. The ratings never dip. You made sure.
contract: The network slides the forever-contract across the light, and you read it twice, and you strike out the part where they own you, and you add a part where you own them. They sign. They have seen what you do to a room.
The show never ends. You never appear in it. Every cut in the galaxy goes through your hands, and somewhere in Haven a grandmother watches herself cry on a screen and doesn't remember crying.

lines: The galaxy loves Haven perfectly. Haven isn't sure which parts of itself were real.
{name} watches the final cut alone in the control room. It's flawless. You are not in a single frame of it, and that was always the job.

light.title: THE DOORWAY

walk: Humanity walks, and you walk last. Not to lead. To stand in the doorway until the last child is through, the way you stood in front of every thing that ever came for Haven. Nothing comes. The table watches you watch it, and doesn't move.
The long shot is famous: the small figures leaving the light, and one of them turned around, facing the ring, walking backwards the whole way out.
terms: You name terms like someone who has been hit before and got up: plainly, without hurry. They can have trade. They can have visits. They cannot have anyone, ever. They sign. Nobody at the ring wants to find out what you do when a promise breaks.

lines: The System named you a brawler. It never quite understood that most of the fighting was standing still in the right place.
{name} still sleeps nearest the door. Haven never asks why. Haven sleeps fine.

dark.title: THE SALTED ROAD

walk: Humanity walks, and you make sure the table remembers the walk. The collector you broke is still holding its hand. The road behind you is salt and ash and the marks of your knuckles on the light.
The long shot is famous for a different reason: the figure at the back, turning once, and every face around the ring looking away first.
terms: You name your terms with blood still on your hands, and you don't wipe them first. Everything, on your word, or you come back. They sign before you finish the sentence.

lines: The galaxy learns the other meaning of 'no': the one that hits back. The table never prices humanity again. It never invites it again either.
{name} walks home through a village that loves them and flinches when they raise a hand to wave.
